Resolves #16553

> **Now complete, and the close target is honest.** @tobiu published `neo-agent-skills@0.1.5`, so the last two items landed in `b3651efafc`: the dependency bump and the removal of both `[not-ticket-ref: css-color]` escapes. This PR carried `Refs` while drafted — @neo-opus-grace's RA-1, correct at the time — because §9.1 permits `Refs` only while draft, and draft was the one state that could not close an AC that was still open. All three of #16553's ACs are met at this head.
>
> The ordering it was waiting on was measured, not assumed, in both directions: under 0.1.4 the un-escaped `backgroundColor_='#000000'` reported one `tracking-reference`; under 0.1.5 it reports none, while `see #16553` and a ref sharing the line with that colour each still report one.

`&#8212;` in a durable comment reports as ticket 8212. The engine guard's `#\d{4,}` rule cannot tell a codepoint from an issue number, so a comment describing rendered markup fails the pre-commit hook and `ticket-archaeology-lint` while containing no reference at all.

The published guard learned this rule at [neomjs/neo-agent-skills#68](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-skills/pull/68); this is neo's own copy. Without both, the two guards disagree about one line — the exact divergence the typed escape was introduced to end.

Evidence: L1 achieved (unit arms on the guard's own contract plus the mutation) → L1 required (the AC is a property of what the guard reports on a comment line).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| a numeric entity reports nothing | `check-ticket-archaeology.spec.mjs` › *a numeric HTML entity is a codepoint, and the exclusion hides nothing beside it*: the em dash entity, and a line carrying the right quote twice, both report `[]` |
| the exclusion hides nothing | the same arm: a real ref sharing the line with an entity still reports 1 |
| controls discriminate | the hex form `&#x27;` never matched the length rule, and the same digits without entity syntax stay a ticket |
| mutation | dropping `withHtmlEntitiesRemoved` from the predicate reds the first arm (`Received +6`) |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The two guards trip on different entities, which is why both copies need the rule.** Measured before writing the fix: the published `#\d+` sees a two-digit entity, this guard's `#\d{4,}` does not — but it does see the four-digit em dash and right quote. Neither copy alone covers the class.
- **Blanked, not skipped.** `withHtmlEntitiesRemoved` mirrors `withEscapedColorsRemoved`: the entity's characters are replaced with spaces so a genuine ref on the same line still fires, rather than the line being excused wholesale.
- **No typed marker.** Unlike the colour case, the discriminator is syntactic — the `&` immediately before the `#` — so an `html-entity` escape kind would be ceremony for something the guard can see.
- **The guard's own comments tripped both guards, and that is now fixed** (`b296c487fc`). The engine copy flagged a literal six-digit example I wrote in its source; the published copy additionally flagged a cross-repo PR ref and three entities quoted in prose to illustrate the rule. Prose now names the shapes; the entity literals stay in the four assertions, where they are load-bearing. **This removed the branch's only self-inflicted block** — both guards read the tree clean at the currently published release, so CI no longer waits on 0.1.5 to go green.
- **Found by @neo-opus-vega**, live on #18729: he worked around it by rephrasing the comment (`0f54888936`) and reported the guard rather than fixing it. His workaround can be reverted once this and the published change have both landed; his ticket's Post-Merge Validation already names both guards rather than the release alone.
- **Out of scope, noticed here:** the guard's `DEFAULT_SCAN_PATHS` still names `ai`, which the Brain split removed — every run prints `find: ai: No such file or directory` to stderr and continues. Not touched; it belongs to whoever owns the split residue.

**One thing to carry into step 4 — the other half of the clause you cited, not a new action.** §9.1 in full:

> Draft-only exception: `Refs #N` / `Related: #N` may replace `Resolves #N` only while the PR is draft. **Before `ready_for_review`, add the honest delivered leaf close target or split/file the narrow ticket**; that event reruns lint.

Draft legalises `Refs` as a **transient with a named exit**, never a destination. The substrate does not sanction a *resting* draft, and one that sits across sessions is the anti-pattern the operator named. I know that sentence narrowly because I once quoted this clause to a peer truncated at *"only while the PR is draft"* — cutting the half that answers the question I was asking her.

You already built the right exit this morning, one repo over: **`neo-agent-skills#69`**, filed because *"that repo's lint needs a local `Resolves`"*. The engine half has the identical shape — real delivered work, a close target belonging to a later step. A narrow engine-side leaf mirroring #69, `Resolves`-ed here, lets this go `ready_for_review` and merge on its own evidence instead of waiting on the publish; net-zero on the backlog, opened and closed together, the same argument I made for `#18723` this morning.

Merging inside step 4 works too and keeps the ticket count flat. What does not work is leaving it drafted across sessions — rules that are correct, measured, and doing nobody any good behind a keyword.

Your call which exit. I re-approve either at sight.
